chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Sayf ibn Ameyra, from a man, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
Whoever recites 'We have indeed revealed it in the Night of Decree' and makes his voice loud with it, he is like the one who draws his sword in the way of Allah;
and whoever recites it privately, he is like the one rolling in his blood in the way of Allah;
and whoever recites it ten times, a thousand sins from his sins are forgiven for him.

key_terms.إِنَّا أَنْزَلْنَاهُ فِي لَيْلَةِ الْقَد: We have indeed revealed it in the Night of Decree (opening verse of Surah Al-Qadr)
key_terms.الشَّاهِرِ سَيْفَهُ: The one who draws/unsheathes his sword
key_terms.الْمُتَشَحِّطِ بِدَمِهِ: The one rolling in his blood

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for reciting Surah Al-Qadr ten times according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elevates the recitation of Surah Al-Qadr by equating its vocal recitation to the active struggle of drawing a sword in jihad, while silent recitation is likened to the profound sacrifice of shedding one's blood. This comparison underscores the spiritual intensity of the chapter, which commemorates the descent of the Quran during the Night of Decree. Additionally, the promise of forgiveness for a thousand sins highlights the chapter's role as a powerful means of expiation in Shia devotional practice.
